stats.label: Minutes to refocus after an interruption

blocks.text: Managing Zoom meetings efficiently on your Mac

As a program coordinator, you likely spend a large portion of your day in meetings. Zoom is the primary stage for your work. You need to manage participants, share documents, and record sessions without breaking your flow. macOS provides tools to help, but the interface can get crowded. Using keyboard shortcuts is the fastest way to keep control. For example, press ⌘ ⇧ M to mute everyone in a meeting if you are the host. This prevents background noise from disrupting your presentation.
Why Zoom for program coordinators on Mac requires preparation

Many coordinators face technical hurdles during live calls. Common issues include incorrect microphone selection or permissions blocking your camera. Always check your System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera to ensure Zoom has access. If you find yourself fumbling for settings, ask Lazur to walk you through it. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where to find the waiting room settings. Lazur will point at the correct menu item on your screen. This saves you from digging through menus while participants wait.
Practical tips for your daily Zoom workflow

items: Always test your audio before the meeting starts by going to Zoom > Settings > Audio.
Use the Waiting Room feature to control who enters your call, keeping sensitive meetings secure.
If you share your screen, remember to check the Share Sound box if you are playing video content.
Keep your Zoom client updated to the latest version to avoid compatibility issues with macOS.
Use local recordings if you need to manage file storage manually on your Mac.

blocks.text: If you struggle to remember keyboard shortcuts, keep a small cheat sheet near your monitor. Lazur can also help by answering questions about specific shortcuts if you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask.
blocks.title: Shortcut mastery

blocks.text: Research shows it takes 23 minutes to refocus after an interruption. In a coordination role, you are interrupted constantly. When you are in a Zoom call, use the Do Not Disturb mode on your Mac. Go to Control Center > Focus > Do Not Disturb. This prevents Slack pings or email alerts from showing up on your screen while you share it with others.
Using Lazur to assist your Zoom sessions

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. It is designed to help you without taking over. When you need to find a setting, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask. Lazur will point to the button or menu you need. If you need to draft a quick follow-up email after a call, hold fn and dictate your notes. Lazur types them out at your cursor in any app, like Outlook or Notion.
Common mistakes to avoid in Zoom

items: Forgetting to mute your microphone when a participant is presenting.
Leaving sensitive browser tabs open when you start a screen share.
Running Zoom on battery power during long meetings, which can throttle performance.
Not checking the camera angle before joining a high-stakes call.
Ignoring macOS permission prompts that prevent Zoom from working correctly.

blocks.text: Keeping your Mac performance high for Zoom

Zoom can be resource-intensive. If your Mac feels slow, check your Activity Monitor. Press ⌘ Space, type Activity Monitor, and press Enter. Look at the CPU tab to see if Zoom or other apps are using too many resources. Close unused apps before your meetings start. This is especially important for Intel-based Macs, which may struggle more than Apple Silicon models with virtual backgrounds.

faq.question: How can I improve my Zoom performance on an older Mac?
faq.answer: Close background applications and ensure you are running the latest version of macOS. Avoid using resource-heavy features like virtual backgrounds if you notice lag.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me in Zoom?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at buttons and guides you, but it does not click or operate the app for you.

faq.question: What is the best way to manage meeting recordings?
faq.answer: Change your recording location in Zoom settings to a dedicated folder on your Mac so you can find them easily later.
